drills.hint: ser: soy, eres, es. Use it for identity and origin.

drills.q: 'You have' (informal tú, from tener) in Spanish?
drills.hint: tener is e→ie: tengo, tienes, tiene.
Regular -ar nosotros ending is -amos.
Regular -er/-ir él preterite ends in -ió, with an accent.
ser and ir share this form: fui, fuiste, fue.

drills.q: 'They will do/make' (future of hacer) in Spanish?
drills.hint: Irregular future stem har- + endings; ellos takes -án.
Feminine but takes el for sound: el agua fría.
A female friend is amiga.
Regular -ar verb; a shop is la tienda.
Feminine: la casa. En casa = at home.
Same word also means 'morning' (la mañana).

drills.q: Fill in: '___ libro' (the book, masculine singular 'the')?
drills.hint: Definite articles: el/la/los/las. Libro is masculine.
Indefinite articles: un/una/unos/unas. Mesa is feminine.
Words ending in a consonant add -es, and the article becomes las.

drills.q: 'It' referring to 'el libro' as a direct object (I read ___)?
drills.hint: Direct object pronouns: lo/la/los/las, placed before the verb: lo leí.
11–15 are single words: once, doce, trece, catorce, quince.

drills.q: How do you say 'It's 2:30' in Spanish?
drills.hint: Use son las for all hours except one (es la una); media = half.

drills.q: How do you say 'Thank you very much' in Spanish?
drills.hint: gracias is feminine plural, so 'much' agrees: muchas.

drills.q: How do you ask 'How much does it cost?' in Spanish?
drills.hint: For plural items use ¿cuánto cuestan? (cost from costar, o→ue).

drills.q: How do you say 'I don't understand' in Spanish?
drills.hint: entender is e→ie: entiendo. Put no before the verb.
